title: Dr. Ariel Ostad: Neuromodulator Assessment with Jeuveau
caption:
Dr. Ariel Ostad walks through his assessment of a patient before treatment with Jeuveau, evaluating facial anatomy, muscle movement, and expression. His individualized approach focuses on softening expression lines while preserving natural movement and facial balance.

---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Visit our official website –
http://www.drarielostad.com/

----------------------------------------------------------------------------
transcript: When I assess a patient for neurotoxin treatment, I begin by looking at the face as a whole. Every muscle has a function and many of these muscles work in opposition to one another. So before deciding where to treat, I want to understand how the patient's face moves naturally. What I want patients to understand is that neuromodulator treatment isn't simply about chasing individual lines. With Juvo, the goal is to temporarily reduce the muscle activity responsible for the moderate to severe globular lines and therefore improve their appearance. So ultimately, I want my patients to still look like themselves. And the goal isn't to eliminate expression altogether, it's to use our understanding of facial anatomy, therefore maintain that natural movement and balance. Juvo temporarily improves the look of moderate to severe frown lines between the eyebrows and adults. There are risks of treatment. Effects of Juvo may spread hours to weeks after injection, causing serious symptoms. Alert your doctor right away at difficulty swallowing, speaking, breathing, eye problems, or muscle weakness, which can be signs of a life-threatening condition. If this happens, do not drive a car, operate machinery, or do other dangerous activities. For complete safety information, see at Juvo way of a lispi or visit evillisrx.com. Ask your doctor if Juvo is right for you.

transcript: Hoje falaremos de um assunto bastante polêmico. O uso de skincare em crianças na faixa etária de 6 a 13 anos de idade. Percompanhe este vídeo para que a gente possa conversar e esclavecer um pouco mais sobre esse assunto. No final do ano passado, um dos predentes mais cobiçados de Natal entre crianças abaixo de 13 anos, por um kit de uma marca chamada Drunk Elephant, que possuía tons muito vibrantes, produtos, crênes de skincare e exercir um fascínio entre as crianças. Esse fenômeno ficou conhecido como Sephora Kids pela presença maciça de crianças e adolescentes em redes de cosméticos de maquiagens em geral. Além disso, o surgimento de meninas entre 1, 8, 12 anos publicando vídeos influenciadores na internet com o uso de maquiagens e skincare de até 10 etapas. Essa situação tem preocupado muitos dermatologistas, pois certos produtos podem causar irritações, grandes sensibilidades da pele de crianças e é muito importante que a criança receba uma orientação de um dermatologista para que saiba o protetor ideal e também o que usar, por exemplo, sabonetes neutros, líquidos e hidratações específicas para cada idade e não usar produtos de adultos, por exemplo. Alguns produtos também podem construir essências corantes e conservantes podendo comprometer o sistema endócrilo da criança em formação. Se você tem filhos ou filhas com uma faixetária entre os seus 8, 12, 13 anos de idade, procure um dermatologista para uma orientação correta. Não deixe que a criança use qualquer produto, principalmente esse automidique. caption:
Exosome treatments are getting a lot of attention, but there are some important things to understand before booking 👀

From the evidence behind their benefits to product quality, safety and regulation, not all exosome treatments are the same.

Before investing in a trending treatment, make sure you understand exactly what you’re being offered and whether it’s appropriate for you.

#Exosomes #ExosomeTreatment #SkinTreatments #AestheticMedicine #SkinHealth
transcript: Before you book an exosome treatment, watch this video because as a cosmetic dermatologist, I'm going to tell you the truth. Exosomes are what we call vesicles. So these are like microcapsules that were thought to transfer messages within cells. So initially we thought there were like waste products within the cells, but they actually transfer messages. So almost like cell signaling within these exosomes, you can load it with cargo. So you can tell a cell what to do. You might tell a cell to reduce inflammation, therefore help things like reduce melanin transfer to help with breaking down pigmentation. Rebuild the barrier. So help with skin barrier. So you can load it with whatever you like. It's really important that when you look at exosome treatments, you ask the person that's treating you, where is this exosome from? Plant-based exosomes are legal in the UK. Animal-based exosomes are not. And which plant is really important? So for example, ASCII, the manufacturer of rose plant exosome, they use the rose plant because it had the most mRNA and RNA transcripts or the same as human skin. So you're going to get more of a chain. Some people are just using random plants just because they sound good without any research to show that they're similar to human skin and therefore would make a difference. There are also some that are derived from animal origin, but there are some safety problems in terms of purification process as well. So really be careful about your exosome and where they're from and who is treating you. Within skincare is super important. In my skincare, we've got different exosomes for different things. So we've got vitamin C exosomes to help with the stability. We've got Apple exosomes, which are great for pigmentation. And then we've got Centella Asiatic exosomes, which are great for redness. Always look at companies that make specific exosomes for specific problem and look at the purity levels because you want to know what's going into your skin. Don't forget to save this before your next exosome appointment. It's super important. If you want advice on the best exosomes, let me know in the comments below and I'll get back to you.

title: Dr. Ariel Ostad Explains the Science Behind Injectable Treatments
caption:
Dr. Ariel Ostad explains the science behind dermal fillers and neurotoxins, from how fillers add volume and support facial contours to how neurotoxins reduce targeted muscle activity to soften expression lines.

---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Visit our official website –
http://www.drarielostad.com/

---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Get social with us –

Facebook - https:
transcript: Hi everyone. I just wanted to spend a few minutes and talk to you about how neuromodulators and hyaluronic acid injectables actually work. What are they doing? Part of the aging process is that we have expression lines and that's primarily on the upper third of the face. So we get what we call 11s. These are frown lines. We get forehead creases, the horizontal lines. We get crow's feet and these are all due to overuse of these muscles over time. As these muscles get stronger they're pulling on the skin leading to lines. So what Juvo as a neuromodulator does is that it blocks the signal from the nerve to the muscle and basically blocks the action of a neurotransmitter called acetylcholine which is a signal that the nerve produces to have a muscle relax. So that's an important distinction. Specifically Juvo I love because it to me it's much more precise. It lasts longer. The onset of action is really faster. With regards to hyaluronic acid injectables as we age we lose collagen and collagen is made up of hyaluronic acid. It's basically a series of sugar molecules and as we age those diminish. So we're taking hyaluronic acid injectables as a form of an injection and filling increases whether it be laugh lines, marionette lines. For some patients who are getting hollowing on their cheekbones we're injecting that in there and therefore they're adding volume. So they're at volumizers that enhance how someone looks. It can be used to soften lines but it can also be used to improve gels, lift up the jawline and just make someone look what they used to look like 10-15 years ago because they had more volume in their skin.
